source.title_on_document: Generative AI in creative education: baseline-linked evidence on learning processes, artistic performance, and authorship

supplement.holds: Supplementary Material S1, the questionnaire instrument. All regression and propensity-score results are in the main text (Figure 4, Tables 4 to 11).

paper_design_summary: Observational course data from 133 undergraduate art students in four intact classes (Character Design and Animation Concept Design) at Communication University of Zhejiang, China. Students chose whether and how much to use AI and self-reported it after the final project (74 AI users under the main definition). Two instructors blind to AI use scored the final artworks on creativity, aesthetic quality, technique, authorship, and completion (0 to 20 each), and the paper relates AI use to these scores with baseline-adjusted OLS, propensity-score matching, and inverse-probability weighting.

studies.label: Course data, four intact undergraduate art classes (final creative project)

assignment.quote: the analysis was conducted in a real course setting at a single institution, using a course-based sample rather than an experimentally assigned design.

participants.exclusions: 151 students in the four classes; one duplicated questionnaire removed (136 retained); three incomplete responses excluded; 133 valid cases. AI users = 74 under the main definition (ai_use = 1).
participants.who: Undergraduate art students (38 first-year, 34 second-year, 61 third-year; animation major and illustration and comic art track) in Character Design and Animation Concept Design courses

ai_tool.name_model: not named; students self-reported AI tool types
ai_tool.how_used: Self-selected use during the creative project. Measured by self-estimates: ai_help_pct (perceived share of AI assistance in ideation, reference search, revision, process organization, technique learning; mean 19.632, SD 20.539) and ai_content_pct (perceived share of the final output directly generated or substantially shaped by AI; mean 12.158, SD 17.412). pp. 6-7, Section 3.1.3; p. 12, Table 3.

task.description: Course creative projects (character design and animation concept design) under a unified theme on traditional cultural topics such as intangible cultural heritage and historical artifacts; final artworks scored by two instructors blind to AI use on five 20-point dimensions (inter-rater kappa 0.92).

outcomes.name: Final total score (sum of five dimensions, 0-100)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Final total is the sum of the five instructor-rated dimensions (0-100; p. 5, Section 3.1.2). The supplementary performance_change analysis uses final_total − baseline_score, where baseline_score = (daily_score + mid_score) / 2 (p. 7, Section 3.2, Equations (1), (3), and (4)). Baseline and final assessments were related but not identical; the change score is a supplementary course-performance indicator, not an experimental gain score or an outcome produced after AI removal. PSM Matched N counts unique matched controls (p. 14, Table 4 note).

contrasts.reported: Baseline-adjusted standardized coefficients: AI use -0.01; assistive use 0.08; content-generative use -0.13 (Figure 4). PSM ATT -1.581, 95% CI -4.297, 0.946; IPW ATE -1.094, 95% CI -4.028, 2.063; Treated N 74, Matched N 30 (Table 4)

Supplementary performance_change = final_total − baseline_score. Baseline-adjusted standardized regression coefficients: AI use -0.01; assistive use 0.07; content-generative use -0.12 (none marked significant; Figure 4, Change row). PSM ATT -1.196, 95% CI [-4.075, 1.473]; IPW ATE 0.129, 95% CI [-2.560, 2.877]; Treated N 74, Matched N 30 (unique matched controls; Table 4, Change row). These are supplementary observational adjusted comparisons.

eligibility.reason: AI use was self-selected and self-reported, not randomly assigned (p. 5, Section 3.1.1; p. 24, Section 7), so criterion 1 is not met. The analyzed sample comprises 133 students (p. 5, Section 3.1.1; p. 10, Table 1), meeting criterion 2. Instructors scored submitted artworks, including originality and distinctiveness in the Creativity rubric (p. 5, Section 3.1.2), meeting criterion 3. The nonrandomized AI-user comparisons with baseline and propensity-score adjustment belong in observational context rather than the core dataset. No diversity or similarity outcome is reported.

one_line_finding: In this observational sample of 133 undergraduate art students in China, self-reported AI users (74) showed no statistically clear adjusted difference from non-users on instructor-rated creativity (originality; baseline-adjusted standardized regression coefficient -0.01, Figure 4, p. 13) or final total score (PSM ATT -1.581, 95% CI -4.297 to 0.946, Table 4, p. 14), while AI use was associated with lower authorship scores (PSM ATT -1.270, 95% CI -1.892 to -0.743, Table 4, p. 14).
